sections.html:
Property tax in Pulaski County runs through Somerset. The PVA (Property Valuation Administrator) puts a number on every parcel; call (606) 679-1812. The sheriff's tax office mails your bill and takes your money, weekdays 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM, with email at taxes@pulaskisheriff.com.

Rates are not set by either one. The fiscal court, the school board and other districts each choose a levy, and your bill adds them up. Pulaski County, Somerset Independent and Science Hill Independent are the three school systems here, so your address decides which school levy lands on you.

The sheriff also bills tangible property, franchise and gas taxes, undeveloped land, oil, and limestone, sand and gravel. Owning a mix of these? Ask whether every item arrives on a separate statement.

When you list a house, keep a folder with the current bill, last year's receipt and the PVA's phone number handy. Buyers and title agents ask for the same papers, and having them ready saves a few days.

Mailing starts in early October. What you owe depends on the day you pay, and the 5 percent January charge matches KRS 134.015.

Pulaski County sheriff: amount owed by payment date
When paidAmount
October 1 to November 1Bill less a 2 percent discount
November 2 to December 31Base amount
January 1 to January 31Base amount plus 5 percent
February 1 to April 15Base amount plus 21 percent
April 16 onwardPay the County Clerk, (606) 679-2042

Walk-in payers can hand over cash, a check or a card (cards add a small fee). Installments are turned down, so show up with the entire balance. Mailing a check? Tuck in a stamped self-addressed envelope and a receipt comes back. Misplaced your bill? Replacements cost nothing.

Somerset is the seat, and Burnside, Eubank, Ferguson and Science Hill round out the towns. Population was estimated at 67,384 in July 2025, a 3.6 percent climb since 2020. Owners occupy 72.5 percent of the 26,210 households. Typical home value is $166,900, and typical gross rent is $803. Only 129 building permits were issued in 2025, which leaves resale houses doing most of the work.

Lake Cumberland and its houseboat trade pull buyers to the south end. US 27 and Kentucky 80 cross the county, Interstate 75 sits about 28 miles east, and Lexington is 76 miles north. A house with roof, septic or shoreline trouble can go to a direct cash buyer, with any tax owed settled at closing.

sections.h2: Homestead exemption and the state rate
sections.html:
Frankfort set the 2025 state rate at 10.6 cents per hundred dollars of assessed value. Your local districts pile their rates on top, and only your own bill shows the final sum.

Homeowners who are 65 or older, or totally disabled, may deduct $49,100 for 2025 and 2026. File through the PVA at (606) 679-1812. Because the state adjusts the figure, check which amount applies this year.

The 2 percent early-payment discount covers the whole bill, not part of it. A seller still on title in October gets it by paying before November 2, and a buyer who closes later in the year inherits whatever is left on the bill.

Value looks too high to you? Begin at the PVA office, whether the parcel is a Lake Cumberland cottage or a farm near Eubank. The appeal cannot be filed before that sit-down. The assessment roll sits open for thirteen days from the first Monday in May. During the meeting the PVA walks you through the math, then writes down what you claim, what was agreed and how it ended.

  • File with the clerk on the workday right after the roll closes.
  • Neighbors who own property sit on the local board, which meets roughly thirty days afterward for as many as five days.
  • Bring paper proof: land and building descriptions, insurance policies, what construction cost, and sales listings. A file with none of these is thrown out.
  • If someone speaks for you, they must appear on the statutory list and hold your signed authorization.

Bills can print before the board decides. If the final value lands above your claim, a supplemental bill covers the gap.

sections.h2: Who owes the tax when a house sells mid year?
sections.html:
The fall bill belongs to whoever held the parcel on January 1, even if a closing prorates it between buyer and seller. Your closing attorney drafts the split in the contract, and a quick call to the tax office tells you if the parcel shows paid or open.

Under KRS 134.015 the tax is a personal debt of the January 1 owner. Under KRS 134.420 the lien sticks to the land for eleven years. Lenders with escrow accounts normally pay what they receive, yet the responsibility stays with you. Moved lately? Forward your bill to the lender.

Moving away? Tell the PVA right away. The older owner deduction follows the person, so the buyer must file a fresh application.

On April 16 unpaid bills leave the sheriff's hands and land with the County Clerk as certificates of delinquency, each backed by a lien. An investor who buys one collects the tax, 12 percent a year, and costs like attorney and filing fees. Your house is not auctioned at this point.

The clerk charges 1 percent a month. Once notices go out, the county attorney's commission and postage join the total. The law puts the sale between 90 and 135 days after transfer. Pay the clerk before that day and no investor can take the bill.

Owing tax does not kill a sale. It just gets paid at the closing table. Here is how to line it up.

  • Get a written payoff for each open year. The sheriff has it until April 15, and the County Clerk has it after.
  • Give the number to your closing attorney so it can be subtracted from your proceeds.
  • If an investor already bought the bill, the payoff comes from that holder, with interest and costs included.
  • Scan the title for a lien ahead of signing, since liens travel with the land from one owner to the next.

A cash sale of a house in rough shape follows the same path, only faster. The buyer skips repairs and lender approval, and the tax debt is paid from your sale money when papers are signed. Bring your latest bill, your deed and a photo ID to the closing office. One week before closing, ring the tax office again so the payoff figure is current.

faqs.q: Can I pay a Pulaski County tax bill by card?
faqs.a: Yes, at the sheriff's counter, with a small surcharge for cards. Cash and checks are fine too. Bring the full amount, since installments are refused.

faqs.q: What are the extra charges after January in Pulaski County?
faqs.a: January costs an extra 5 percent. From February 1 to April 15 the extra is 21 percent. Once April 16 arrives, you pay the County Clerk.

faqs.q: When does the Pulaski County early discount apply?
faqs.a: Pay between October 1 and November 1 and 2 percent comes off. From November 2 to December 31 the plain base amount applies.

faqs.q: Where do I claim the older owner deduction in Pulaski County?
faqs.a: Phone the PVA at (606) 679-1812 to file. It takes $49,100 off the assessment for owners 65 and up, or totally disabled, in 2025 and 2026.

faqs.q: Will the sheriff auction my house over unpaid Pulaski County tax?
faqs.a: Not at the sheriff stage. After April 15 the clerk can sell the bill to an investor, who then holds a lien earning 12 percent a year plus costs.
